p.src: Now the neighbors seized Old Wang and took him straight to Ji Prefecture to report the matter. The prefect had just taken his seat in court when the whole party knelt and reported, “This old fellow was carrying a shoulder load of rice cakes and gruel when he spilled it on the ground. When we looked, there were two corpses lying there—one a monk and the other a mendicant friar. Neither had a stitch on his body, and a knife lay beside the friar.” The old man pleaded, “I earn my living selling rice cakes and gruel every day, and I always go out at the fifth watch to seek customers. This morning I rose a little earlier, and as I walked along with this iron-headed monkey, I failed to watch the ground, tripped, and smashed all my bowls and dishes. Then I saw two blood-soaked corpses lying there. In my sudden fright I cried out, only to be seized by the neighbors and dragged before the authorities. I beg Your Honor to examine the matter with mirror-bright judgment.” The prefect immediately took their depositions and issued an official order appointing the local headmen to lead the coroner and constables, escort the neighbors, Old Wang, and the rest to examine the bodies, and return with a full report. When the examination at the scene was complete, they returned to the prefecture and reported, “The murdered monk is Pei Ruhai, the acharya of Bao'en Temple, while the mendicant beside him is Hu Dao, who lived behind the temple. The monk was completely naked and died from three or four stab wounds on his body. A murderous knife was found beside Hu Dao, and there is a ligature mark around his neck. It appears that Hu Dao drew the knife and stabbed the monk to death, then hanged himself for fear of punishment.” The prefect summoned the monks of the temple and questioned them about the circumstances, but none knew what had happened, leaving him unable to reach a decision. The clerk in charge of the case submitted, “It is plain to see that this monk was stark naked. He and that friar must have been engaged in some indecent and unlawful business and killed each other. Old Wang had nothing to do with it. Have the neighbors provide guarantors and remain available for questioning. Order the temple abbot to prepare coffins at once, encoffin the bodies, and place them elsewhere. Then draw up a document declaring that the two killed each other, and that will settle it.” “That is reasonable,” said the prefect. He thereupon disposed of the cases of all concerned, and no more need be said of it.

p.src: How hateful—the shameless shaven rogue, so wanton and wild in his deeds! He secretly wooed a lovely woman, hoping they might wed and forever share the mandarin-duck bed. But his accumulated sins had reached their fullness; after disgracing so many monks, he lay a corpse in a pool of blood in the street. Today he lies stark naked—a pretty sight indeed! He never thought of the patriarchs in the sutras, standing waist-deep in snow or offering themselves to tigers from a cliff. Mulian saved his mother and raised her to heaven; this thieving baldhead lost his life for a woman.

p.src: A lecherous monk invited death’s retribution; in the dark, the reckoning missed not by a hair. The friar’s corpse, too, was a curious thing: truly without a thread upon him, he met the butcher’s blade where he stood. The senior monk has now spent his vital essence and blood; the junior monk enjoyed last night’s amorous sport. Within the Buddhist gate, bosom friends met with severed throats; fighting to the death to share one grave, they threw away two lingering lives.

p.src: At the Ji Prefecture offices, Yang Xiong heard the report that the monk and the friar had been killed. He understood seven or eight parts of the truth at once and thought, “This must surely be Shi Xiu’s doing. The other day I wronged him in a moment of folly. I have some leisure today, so I shall seek him out and ask him the truth.” Just as he was passing the prefectural bridge, he heard someone call from behind, “Brother, where are you going?” Yang Xiong turned and saw Shi Xiu. “Brother,” he said, “I was just wondering where to find you.” “Come to my lodgings first, brother,” said Shi Xiu. “I have something to tell you.” He led Yang Xiong into a small room at the inn and said, “Brother, did I lie to you?” “Do not blame me, brother,” said Yang Xiong. I was stupid for a moment and acted wrongly. I spoke rashly after drinking and let that woman deceive me instead. No wonder you quarreled with me. I came especially to find you today and humbly beg your forgiveness.” Shi Xiu said, “Though I am a man of no great ability, brother, I am still an upright hero who stands between heaven and earth. How could I ever do such a thing? I feared you might fall prey to a treacherous scheme later, so I came looking for you. I have tokens here for you to see. I brought away all the clothes stripped from the monk and the friar; they are here.” At the sight of them, anger flared in Yang Xiong’s heart. “Forgive me, brother,” he said. Tonight I shall cut that vile woman to pieces and vent this bitter rage.” Shi Xiu laughed. “There you go again. You work in the public offices. How can you not know the law? You have not caught her in the very act of adultery, so how can you kill her? If by chance I were talking nonsense, would you not have killed someone unjustly?” “Then how can I possibly let the matter rest?” asked Yang Xiong. Shi Xiu replied, “Just follow my instructions, brother, and I shall show you how to act as a true man.” “Brother, how will you show me how to act as a true man?” asked Yang Xiong. Shi Xiu said, “Outside the eastern gate stands Mount Cuiping, a very secluded place. Tomorrow, say only, ‘It has been a long time since I offered incense, so today I shall go there with your sister-in-law.’ Lure the woman out and bring Ying’er along with you to the mountain. I shall wait there beforehand. Face-to-face, we will settle every point of right and wrong. Then you can write her a letter of divorce and cast her off. Would that not be the best course?” Yang Xiong said, “There is no need for you to explain further, brother. I know now that you are innocent and that it was all the woman’s lies.” “No,” replied Shi Xiu. “I also want you to learn the truth about her dealings.” Yang Xiong said, “Since this is your wise plan, brother, it cannot be wrong. I shall bring that vile woman without fail tomorrow. Be sure you are not late.” Shi Xiu replied, “If I fail to come, then everything I have said is false.”

p.src: Yang Xiong then took leave of Shi Xiu, departed the inn, and went to attend to his duties at the prefectural offices. When he returned that evening, he did not raise the matter or say anything at all, but behaved exactly as he did every day. At daybreak the next morning, he rose and said to the woman, “Last night I dreamed that a divine being called to me and said I had not yet fulfilled an old vow. Long ago I vowed to offer incense at the Temple of the Sacred Peak outside the eastern gate, but I have never redeemed that vow. I have some leisure today and mean to fulfill it, so you must come with me.” “Go and fulfill it yourself,” said the woman. “What use is there in my going?” Yang Xiong replied, “I made this vow when our marriage was first arranged, so you must come with me.” “If that is so,” said the woman, “let us eat an early vegetarian meal, heat water, bathe, and then go.” Yang Xiong said, “I shall go buy incense and paper offerings and hire a sedan chair. Bathe, dress your hair, put on your ornaments, and wait for me. Tell Ying’er to come along as well.”

p.src: Yang Xiong arranged matters with Shi Xiu, bought paper offerings and candles, and returned home to eat breakfast. The woman knew nothing of the matter and concerned herself only with dressing immaculately. Ying'er also put on her finery, while the bearers brought the sedan chair and were already waiting outside the door. Yang Xiong said, “Father-in-law, please mind the house. My wife and I will return as soon as we have burned incense.” Pan Gong said, “Burn plenty of incense, and go early and return early.”

p.src: The woman entered the sedan chair, Ying'er followed beside it, and Yang Xiong walked behind. Once they were through the eastern gate, Yang Xiong quietly instructed the bearers, “Carry her up Mount Cuiping for me, and I shall pay you extra.” In less than four hours, they had reached Mount Cuiping. Mount Cuiping lay twenty li beyond Jizhou's eastern gate and was covered entirely with scattered family graves. As far as the eye could see, there was nothing but green grass and white poplars, without a hermitage or temple anywhere. Yang Xiong had the woman carried halfway up the mountain, then told the bearers to set down the chair. He went to the rear, unfastened and raised its curtain, and told her to come out. The woman asked, “Why have we come into these mountains?” Yang Xiong said, “Just keep going up for now. You bearers are to wait here and not follow. In a little while I shall give you even more for wine.” The bearers said, “That is no trouble. We shall simply wait here at your service.” Yang Xiong led the woman and Ying'er up four or five tiers of the slope, where they saw Shi Xiu sitting above them. The woman asked, “Why did you not bring the incense and paper offerings?” Yang Xiong replied, “I sent someone ahead with them.” He led the woman into an ancient burial ground. Shi Xiu set his bundle, waist saber, and staff before the roots of a tree, then came forward and said, “My respects, Sister-in-law.” The woman hurriedly answered, “How is it that you are here too, Brother?” Even as she spoke, she felt a shock of alarm within. Shi Xiu said, “I have been waiting here especially for you for some time.” Yang Xiong said, “The other day you told me that my brother repeatedly teased you with suggestive words, laid his hand upon your breast, and asked whether you were with child. There is no one here today, so the two of you shall confront each other and make the truth plain.” The woman said, “Oh, that is all in the past. Why keep talking about it?” Shi Xiu glared at her and said, “Sister-in-law, what are you saying? This is no idle matter. We must settle it plainly before my brother.” The woman said, “Brother, why dredge that up when nothing came of it?” Shi Xiu said, “Sister-in-law, do not persist in denying it. I shall show you some evidence.” He went to the bundle, took out the clothes belonging to the monk Hai and the mendicant, and spread them on the ground. “Do you recognize these?” he asked. At the sight of them, the woman's face flushed scarlet, and she had no answer. With a hiss, Shi Xiu drew his waist saber and said to Yang Xiong, “We need only question Ying'er about this affair, and the whole truth will be known.”

p.src: Yang Xiong seized the maid, dragged her forward, and forced her to kneel before him. He roared, “You wretched little slut! Tell the whole truth at once: how the adultery began in the monk's quarters, how the appointments were arranged, how the incense table served as the signal, and how you had the mendicant come beating his wooden fish. Tell me honestly and I shall spare your life; but conceal so much as a single word, and I shall first hack you into minced meat.” Ying'er cried, “Master, it was none of my doing! Do not kill me, and I will tell you.” She then recounted how they had drunk wine in the monks' quarters, gone upstairs to see the Buddha's tooth, and driven her downstairs when Pan Gong awoke from his drunkenness. “The two secretly made an arrangement that on the third day the mendicant would come begging for a meal and I was to take some copper coins and give them to him as alms. My mistress agreed with him that whenever you, Master, were spending the night on duty at the prison, I was to carry the incense table outside the back door as their secret signal. When the mendicant saw it, he would go and inform the monk. That night, the monk Hai would disguise himself as a layman, put on a headcloth, and come inside. During the fifth watch, we would hear the mendicant beating his wooden fish and loudly invoking the Buddha as the signal, whereupon I was to open the back door and let the monk out. Whenever the monk came, they could not keep it hidden from me and had no choice but to tell me. My mistress promised me a pair of bracelets and a suit of clothes, so I had no choice but to comply. They came and went like this several dozen times, until the two men were eventually killed. She then gave me several more pieces of jewelry and told me to tell you, Master, that Uncle Shi had teased her with improper words. But I never witnessed any such thing, and therefore did not dare say it. This alone is the truth, and not one word of it is false.”

p.src: The woman had no choice but to recount her affair with the monk, beginning with the night of the Buddhist service and continuing through all their later meetings, telling everything one detail at a time. Shi Xiu said, “Then why did you tell my brother instead that I had tried to seduce you?” The woman said, “The other day, when he was drunk, he cursed me. There was something strange in the way he cursed, and I guessed that you had noticed something suspicious and told him. During the fifth watch, he brought the matter up again and asked about you, so I invented that story to put him off. In truth, you never did any such thing.”

p.src: Yang Xiong said, “Brother, tear the ornaments from this slut's head and strip off her clothes. I shall attend to her myself.” Shi Xiu stripped the woman of all her headdress, jewelry, and clothing. Yang Xiong cut two strips from her skirt and bound her to a tree with his own hands. Shi Xiu also removed all of Ying'er's jewelry, then handed over the saber and said, “Brother, what use is there in leaving this little slut alive? Best root out the grass and destroy the root once and for all.” Yang Xiong answered, “Indeed. Give me the saber, Brother. I shall do it myself.”

p.src: Seeing that matters had taken a deadly turn, Ying'er was just about to cry out when Yang Xiong raised his hand, struck once with the saber, and cut her in two. Bound to the tree, the woman cried, “Brother, plead with him for me!” Shi Xiu said, “Sister-in-law, my brother himself has come to attend to you.”

u.src: Seeing that matters had taken a deadly turn, Ying'er was just about to cry out when Yang Xiong raised his hand, struck once with the saber, and cut her in two.
Bound to the tree, the woman cried, “Brother, plead with him for me!”
Shi Xiu said, “Sister-in-law, my brother himself has come to attend to you.”

p.src: Yang Xiong stepped forward, pried out her tongue with his knife, and cut it off with one stroke so that the woman could no longer cry out. Pointing at her, Yang Xiong cursed, “You vile wretch! For a moment I misheard and failed to understand, and you very nearly deceived me. First, you ruined the bond between me and my brother; second, sooner or later you would surely have taken my life. Better that I strike first today and gain the upper hand. I wonder how the heart, liver, and five organs of a woman like you are formed. Let me take a look.” With one stroke he cut straight from the pit of her heart to below her belly, took out her heart, liver, and entrails, and hung them on a pine tree. Yang Xiong then dismembered the woman into seven parts and tied up her head, face, and clothing in a bundle. Yang Xiong said, “Brother, come here. Let us discuss a sound plan. Now that the adulterer and the faithless woman are both dead, where can you and I go to find refuge?” Shi Xiu said, “I have already thought it through. There is a place for us. Let us set out at once, brother, without delay.” Yang Xiong asked, “And where are we going?” Shi Xiu replied, “You have killed a person, brother, and so have I. If we do not go and join the band at Liangshan Marsh, where else could we turn?” Yang Xiong said, “Wait. Neither of us knows a single person there. Why should they agree to take us in?” Shi Xiu said, “You are mistaken, brother. Everyone in the rivers and lakes now knows that Song Gongming, the ‘Timely Rain’ of Shandong, recruits worthy men and befriends heroes from all beneath heaven. With all the martial skill you and I possess, why worry that they will not take us in?” Yang Xiong said, “In all things it is best to face the difficulties first and the ease afterward, so as to prevent later trouble. Yet I happen to be an officer of the law, and I fear they may suspect us and refuse us shelter.” Shi Xiu laughed. “Did he not begin as a court clerk himself? Let me set your mind completely at ease. On the day you accepted me as your sworn brother, the two men who first drank with me at the tavern were Dai Zong, the ‘Magic Messenger’ of Liangshan Marsh, and Yang Lin, the ‘Brocade Leopard.’ They gave me a ten-tael ingot of silver, which is still in my bundle. Through them, therefore, we can seek refuge there.” Yang Xiong said, “Since we have such a connection, I shall gather some traveling money and then we will leave.” Shi Xiu said, “Brother, how can you be so troublesome? What if the affair comes to light when you enter the city and you are arrested? How would you escape? There are already plenty of hairpins, bracelets, and ornaments in the bundle, and I have some silver as well. It would suffice even for three or five more men, so why go back for anything else? If that stirs up trouble, how could we save ourselves? This affair will soon be discovered. We must not linger; our only course is to flee behind the mountain.”

p.src: Shi Xiu shouldered the bundle and took up his staff; Yang Xiong thrust his waist knife into his belt and picked up his broad-bladed sword. Just as they were about to leave the ancient tomb, a man emerged from behind the pine trees and cried, “In a peaceful age beneath the boundless heavens, you cut a person to pieces and then mean to flee to Liangshan Marsh and join the band. I have been listening for quite some time.” When Yang Xiong and Shi Xiu looked, the man bowed his head to the ground before them. Yang Xiong recognized him. His surname was Shi, his given name Qian, and he was originally from Gaotangzhou, though he had drifted to this place; he made his living there by such deeds as scaling eaves and walls, leaping fences, and stealing horses. He had once faced charges at the Jizhou prefectural court, but Yang Xiong had saved him. Everyone called him the ‘Flea on a Drum.’ A poem bears witness:

p.src: Yang Xiong then asked Shi Qian, “What are you doing here?” Shi Qian replied, “Hear my report, brother warden. Lately I have had no way to make a living, so I have been digging up ancient graves in these hills to find a few things of value. When I saw you conducting your business here, I dared not come out and intrude. But then I heard you say you were going to join the band at Liangshan Marsh. All I can do here now is steal chickens and dogs; when will there ever be an end to it? Would it not be better if I followed you two brothers up the mountain? I do not know whether you would be willing to take me with you?” Shi Xiu said, “Since you are a man fit to rank among heroes, and they are now recruiting brave men there, they will hardly object to one more. If that is how you feel, let us all go together.” Shi Qian said, “I know a bypath that will take us there.” He immediately led Yang Xiong and Shi Xiu down a bypath behind the mountain, and the three of them set off for Liangshan Marsh.

p.src: Meanwhile, the two sedan-chair bearers waited halfway up the mountain until the red sun touched the western horizon. When the three did not return, they recalled their instructions and dared not go up. At last they could bear it no longer and had no choice but to wander up the mountain in search of them. There they saw a great flock of crows clustered around the ancient tomb. When the two bearers went closer to look, they found that the crows were fighting over the entrails and devouring them, which was why they were making such a din. The bearers were horrified by what they saw. They hurried home to report it to Pan Gong, then went with him to lodge an accusation at the Jizhou prefectural court. The prefect at once dispatched a county commandant with a coroner and attendants to Mount Cuiping. After examining the bodies, they returned and reported to the prefect: “We examined the body of the woman Pan Qiaoyun, who was cut apart beside the pine tree, and that of her maid Ying’er, who was killed below the ancient tomb. Beside the grave lay a heap of clothing belonging to a woman, a monk, and a wandering friar.” On hearing this, the prefect recalled the recent affair of Monk Hai and the wandering friar and questioned Pan Gong closely. The old man recounted in detail the episode of the drunkenness in the monk’s quarters and the reason Shi Xiu had left. The prefect said, “It is plain that this woman committed adultery with the monk, while the maid and the wandering friar acted as go-betweens. It seems that when the scoundrel Shi Xiu encountered this injustice, he killed the friar and the monk; and today that scoundrel Yang Xiong undoubtedly killed the woman and her maid. That must be how it happened. Once Yang Xiong and Shi Xiu are captured, we shall know the truth.” He immediately issued official orders and offered reward money for the capture of Yang Xiong and Shi Xiu. The sedan-chair bearers and all the others were released to await further summons. Pan Gong went to buy coffins and had the bodies encoffined and buried; there is no more to tell of that.

p.src: Before it ran the public road, and behind it flowed a broad stream; hundreds of weeping willows faced the gate, while one or two flowering plum trees stood beside the house. A fence of thorn and brush encircled the thatched dwelling; reed blinds covered the earthen sleeping platforms before and behind. Along the wall on the right was written, “At dusk the secluded courtyard receives guests from the Five Lakes;” and on the left were inscribed seven characters: “At dawn the spacious door welcomes travelers from the Three Isles.”

p.src: At dusk that day, just as the waiter was about to shut the door, the three men came barging in. The waiter said, “You gentlemen must have come a long way to arrive so late.” Shi Qian said, “We have traveled more than a hundred li today, which is why we arrived so late.” The waiter admitted the three of them for the night and asked, “Have you gentlemen not cooked your supper?” Shi Qian said, “We shall see to it ourselves.” The waiter said, “There are no other guests staying tonight. Two clean pots are on the stove, so you may use them as you please.” Shi Qian asked, “Do you sell wine and meat here?” The waiter replied, “There was some meat this morning, but the people from the nearby villages bought it all. Only one jar of wine remains, and there is nothing to eat with it.” Shi Qian said, “Very well. First lend us five sheng of rice to cook, and we shall see about the rest afterward.” The waiter brought out rice for Shi Qian, who washed it and set a pot of rice cooking. Meanwhile, Shi Xiu settled their baggage in the room. Yang Xiong took out a hairpin and gave it to the waiter, telling him to bring the jar of wine for them to drink first and settle the entire account the next day. The waiter accepted the hairpin, went inside, carried out the jar, opened it, and placed a dish of cooked vegetables on the table. Shi Qian first fetched a bucket of hot water and had Yang Xiong and Shi Xiu wash their hands and feet. Then, while warming and pouring the wine, he invited the waiter to sit and drink with them, set down four large bowls, filled them, and they began drinking. Seeing more than a dozen fine broad-bladed polearms thrust beneath the inn’s eaves, Shi Xiu asked the waiter, “Why does your inn have all these weapons?” The waiter replied, “They were all left here by our master’s household.” Shi Xiu asked, “What sort of man is your master?” The waiter said, “Sir, you are a traveler of the rivers and lakes. How can you not know the name of this place? That lofty mountain ahead is called Mount Dulong. Before the mountain stands a separate, towering ridge called Dulong Ridge, and our master’s residence is upon it. The land for thirty li around here is called Zhu Family Manor. The lord of the manor, the venerable Zhu Chaofeng, has three sons, known as the Three Champions of the Zhu Clan. Before and behind the manor are five to seven hundred households, all tenant farmers, and every household has been issued two broad-bladed polearms. This place is called the Zhu Family Inn. Dozens of household retainers often lodge here, and that is why these broad-bladed polearms have been assigned to this inn.” Shi Xiu asked, “What use is there in distributing weapons at the inn?” The waiter answered, “Liangshan Marsh is not far from here. They fear its bandits may come to demand grain, so these preparations have been made.” Shi Xiu said, “Suppose I give you some silver. How about getting me one of those broad-bladed polearms to use?” The waiter said, “That cannot be done. Every weapon bears a registered number. A humble fellow like me could not endure the beating my master would give me. My master’s discipline is severe.” Shi Xiu laughed. “I was only teasing you, yet you have already taken fright. Let us just attend to our drinking.” The waiter said, “I can drink no more. I shall retire first; please make yourselves at home and enjoy a few more cups.” The waiter then left.

p.src: Yang Xiong and Shi Xiu drank on for a while. Then Shi Qian asked, “Brothers, would you like some meat?” Yang Xiong said, “The waiter said there was no meat for sale. Where could you have got any?” Shi Qian chuckled and fetched an enormous rooster from the kitchen. Yang Xiong asked, “Where did you get that chicken?” Shi Qian replied, “Just now, when your brother went out back to relieve himself, I saw this chicken in a coop. Thinking there was nothing for my brothers to eat with their wine, I quietly took it to the stream and killed it. When I carried the bucket of hot water out back, I plucked it clean there and cooked it through, then brought it for my two brothers to eat.” Yang Xiong said, “You rascal, your hands and feet are still as thievish as ever.” Shi Xiu laughed. “He has not changed his old trade.” The three laughed awhile, tore the chicken apart with their hands and ate it, serving themselves rice as they did so. The waiter had slept only briefly when uneasiness overcame him. He got up and went about checking the front and rear of the inn. He saw chicken feathers and bones on the kitchen table, and when he looked at the stove, there was half a pot of rich broth. The waiter hurried out back to look in the coop. Finding the chicken gone, he rushed out and demanded, “You gentlemen have no sense of right and wrong! Why did you steal and eat the rooster that announces the dawn for my inn?” Shi Qian said, “What devilry is this? Good heavens! I bought this chicken on the road for us to eat. When did I ever see your chicken?” The waiter asked, “Then where has my chicken gone?” Shi Qian replied, “Perhaps a wildcat dragged it away, a weasel ate it, or a hawk swooped down and carried it off. How should I know?” The waiter said, “My chicken was in the coop just now. If you did not steal it, who did?” Shi Xiu said, “Do not quarrel. Tell us what it was worth, and we shall compensate you.” The waiter said, “Mine was a dawn-crowing rooster, and the inn cannot do without it. Even if you paid me ten taels of silver, it would be no use. I want only my chicken returned.” Shi Xiu flew into a rage. “Whom do you think you can swindle? What will you do if I refuse to compensate you?” The waiter laughed. “You gentlemen had better not come here looking for trouble! My inn is unlike other inns. We shall seize you, take you to the manor, and hand you over as bandits from Liangshan Marsh.” Hearing this, Shi Xiu cursed loudly, “Even if I were a hero of Liangshan Marsh, how could you seize me and claim a reward?” Yang Xiong was also angered. “We offered in good faith to pay you some money. If we refuse, how dare you seize us?” The waiter shouted, “Thieves!” At once, three or five burly men, stripped to the waist, rushed out from inside the inn and charged straight at Yang Xiong and Shi Xiu. Shi Xiu struck out, felling each man with a single punch. Just as the waiter was about to cry out again, Shi Qian slapped him across the face, swelling his cheek and leaving him unable to utter a sound. Those burly men all fled through the back door. Yang Xiong said, “Brothers, those rascals have surely gone to summon help. Let us finish our rice quickly and leave.” The three ate their fill, divided the bundles and tied them around their waists, put on their hemp sandals, buckled on their sabers, and each chose a fine broad-bladed polearm from the rack. Shi Xiu said, “Since things have come to this, we may as well go through with it and spare him nothing.” He went before the stove, found a bundle of straw, kindled it in the fire, and thrust the flames into every corner within. The wind fanned the thatched building, and the flames rose with a fierce crackling roar. In moments, the fire towered as vast as the sky. The three lengthened their strides and hurried away along the main road. Indeed:

Shi Xiu said, “Since things have come to this, we may as well go through with it and spare him nothing.”
He went before the stove, found a bundle of straw, kindled it in the fire, and thrust the flames into every corner within.
The wind fanned the thatched building, and the flames rose with a fierce crackling roar.
In moments, the fire towered as vast as the sky.
The three lengthened their strides and hurried away along the main road.
Indeed:

p.src: All because a thief stole a single fowl, heroic men were set racing in pursuit. Across Liangshan’s watery marsh great waves would rise, and the Zhu Family Manor would be reduced to mire.

u.src: All because a thief stole a single fowl, heroic men were set racing in pursuit.
Across Liangshan’s watery marsh great waves would rise, and the Zhu Family Manor would be reduced to mire.

p.src: The three men had traveled for two watches when they saw countless torches ahead and behind them. Some one or two hundred men came chasing after them, shouting at the tops of their voices. Shi Xiu said, “Do not panic. Let us take a side path.” Yang Xiong said, “Wait. If one comes, we kill one; if two come, we kill the pair. We shall leave when daylight comes.” Before he had finished speaking, the men closed in from every side. Yang Xiong took the lead, Shi Xiu guarded the rear, and Shi Qian stayed between them. Brandishing their broad-bladed staffs, the three engaged the manor retainers. At first, the crowd knew nothing of their prowess and rushed at them, swinging spears and cudgels. Yang Xiong raised his broad-bladed staff and promptly stabbed down five or seven of them. Those in front fled, and those behind hurried to retreat. Shi Xiu charged among them and stabbed down another six or seven men. When the manor retainers all around heard that more than ten men had been wounded or killed, each began fearing for his life. Realizing that matters were going badly, they all withdrew. Whenever the enemy yielded a step, the three pressed forward a step. As they advanced, shouts suddenly rose again. Two grappling hooks shot out from the withered grass; one caught Shi Qian squarely and dragged him into a clump of grass. Shi Xiu wheeled around to rescue Shi Qian, but two more grappling hooks thrust out behind him. Yang Xiong’s quick eyes caught them; he swept them aside with his broad-bladed staff, then stabbed into the grass with it. A shout arose, and the ambushers all fled. Seeing that Shi Qian had been captured, the two feared venturing deeper into dangerous ground and had no heart to prolong the fight. Unable to concern themselves with Shi Qian any longer, they could only search everywhere for a way out. In the distance torches flickered confusedly, while the narrow paths had neither thickets nor trees. They followed whatever way the light revealed and made straight eastward. The manor retainers searched everywhere but could not catch them. They went to tend their wounded, bound Shi Qian’s arms behind his back, and escorted him to the Zhu Family Manor.

p.src: Now Yang Xiong and Shi Xiu walked on until daybreak, when they saw a village tavern. Shi Xiu said, “Brother, let us buy a bowl of wine and some food at the tavern ahead, then ask the way.” The two entered the village tavern, leaned their broad-bladed staffs against the wall, and sat facing each other. They called for the waiter to bring wine and prepare some food. The waiter laid out vegetables and dishes to accompany the wine, then warmed the wine and brought it over. They were just about to eat when a burly man rushed in from outside. He had a broad face, square jowls, bright eyes, and large ears; his features were ugly and his build coarse. He wore a tea-brown silk tunic, a swastika-patterned headcloth, a white silk sash over his shoulder, and a pair of oiled leather boots. He called out, “The master orders you to shoulder the load and deliver it to the manor.” The innkeeper hurriedly replied, “The load is packed. We shall deliver it to the manor shortly.” Having given his instructions, the man turned to leave, adding, “Bring it quickly.” As he was about to go out, he passed directly before Yang Xiong and Shi Xiu. Yang Xiong recognized him and called, “Young fellow, how is it that you are here? Will you not even look at me?” The man turned his head and looked. Recognizing Yang Xiong as well, he cried, “Benefactor, how have you come to this place?” He faced Yang Xiong and bowed before him. Had Yang Xiong not encountered this man, the three manors’ sworn alliance would not have been brought to nothing, nor would the gathered tigers have roared and raised a storm of calamity. Who, after all, was the man whom Yang Xiong and Shi Xiu encountered? Listen to the explanation in the next chapter.
